entities.name: Russian Ground Forces
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Russian Ground Forces (Росси́йские Си́лы Сухопу́тных Во́йск) represent the land warfare component of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation, officially established in 1992 following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. This institution plays a pivotal role in the military strategy of Russia, which is characterized by its extensive territorial expanse and the geopolitical complexities of Eastern Europe. Their headquarters, situated in the Main Building of the Ministry of Defense in Moscow, symbolizes the centralization of military power and reflects Russia’s historical emphasis on a strong land army as a deterrent in international relations.

Since their inception, the Russian Ground Forces have undergone significant transformations, particularly during the conflicts in Chechnya in the 1990s and the subsequent military operations in Georgia in 2008, and most recently in Ukraine beginning in 2014. These operations showcased advancements in military technology, tactics, and the strategic utility of ground forces in modern warfare. The forces have been involved in various military exercises, joint operations, and have engaged in reforms aimed at enhancing their combat readiness and effectiveness, including the transition to a more professional military structure.

The legacy of the Russian Ground Forces extends beyond mere military engagements; it has shaped Russia's national identity and its approach to regional security dynamics. The institutional memory of past conflicts continues to influence contemporary military doctrine and strategy, reinforcing a narrative of resilience and power. Furthermore, the existence and expansion of these ground forces have had significant implications for NATO relations and the security architecture of Europe in the 21st century.
